detail.title: Nonreciprocal Coupling and Coarse-Grained Dissipation Bounds
detail.summary: This research revises thermodynamic dissipation bounds by integrating information-theoretic constraints with memory dynamics in nonequilibrium systems. It establishes that predictive control in information engines is fundamentally limited by the interplay between memory retention energy costs, information-processing speed, and the precision of the underlying physical causal records. Specifically, generalized Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relations (TURs) provide tighter bounds for systems operating under finite-memory or non-equilibrium steady-state conditions compared to original, unconstrained formulations.

detail.title: Nonreciprocal Coupling and Coarse-Grained Dissipation Bounds
detail.summary: Analysis of information engines confirms that dissipation is not only determined by thermal energy but is constrained by the precision of causal memory records. Using generalized TURs, we establish that information-processing engines—especially those utilizing feedback—face lower bounds on energy consumption that are explicitly linked to predictive accuracy and memory state maintenance.
detail.reason: This revision formalizes the integration of Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relations with causal memory mechanics and provides a rigorous grounding for the project's predictive information bounds.
